extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural researchers, grant applicants, peer reviewers, and NIH staff involved in review
extracted.subtask_short: NIH peer review policy and criteria
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of NIH peer review process, roles, and policy documents that govern evaluation and rating of grant applications, including human-subjects, inclusion, and safety-monitoring requirements. Links to specific guidance and proposed regulations are provided for reviewers and applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific and technical merit
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the initial peer review is to evaluate and rate the scientific and technical merit of the proposed research or research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial peer review is conducted by Scientific Review Groups (SRGs) managed by Scientific Review Administrators (SRAs) in NIH Institutes and Centers. Evaluations should focus on the scientific/technical merit of the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-step peer review process (initial SRG then Advisory Councils)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review of applications submitted to the NIH takes place in multiple steps: the initial step in Scientific Review Groups (SRGs) and a second level of peer review carried out by the NIH National Advisory Councils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRGs perform the initial scientific/technical evaluation; National Advisory Councils provide a second-level review to ensure advice from a cross-section of the US population during deliberation and funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management of SRGs by SRAs and NIH components
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Review Groups are managed by Scientific Review Administrators who are located in the Institutes and Centers that are components of the NIH (for example, the Center for Scientific Review and Review Branches of awarding ICs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different NIH components (CSR, IC Review Branches) manage review groups depending on application type (investigator-initiated vs. RFAs or special programs); reviewers and applicants should be aware of referral pathways and management structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency: availability of SRG membership rosters
rubrics_metrics.description: Rosters of the membership of NIH Scientific Review Groups are available for standing review committees as well as Special Emphasis Panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication of rosters supports transparency about who is performing initial peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of NIH National Advisory Councils
rubrics_metrics.description: These Councils are composed of scientists from the extramural research community and public representatives; they ensure that the NIH receives advice from a cross-section of the US population in its deliberation and decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory Councils conduct second-level review and contribute to programmatic and policy considerations beyond initial scientific merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Oversight Group (PROG) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The function of the Peer Review Oversight Group (PROG) is to advise and make recommendations to the Deputy Director for Extramural Research and the Director, NIH, on development and implementation of policies pertaining to monitoring, coordination, and evaluation of peer review conducted at the NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PROG activities include ensuring review processes keep pace with research advances and that reviewer expertise aligns with scientific needs; it also establishes workgroups to address regulatory burdens and inclusion issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of peer reviewer expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewer expertise should be appropriate for the needs of science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PROG is charged with ensuring reviewer expertise is appropriate; selecting reviewers with relevant expertise is an evaluative requirement to ensure quality reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of human subjects — reviewer instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH Instructions to Reviewers for Evaluating Research Involving Human Subjects in Grant and Cooperative Agreement Applications (PDF), April 5, 2002.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should follow the specific NIH instructions when assessing protections for human subjects in applications; linked documents and decision trees provide detailed evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for human and animal subjects research
rubrics_metrics.description: Important Notice to Applicants: Requirements for Human and Animal Subjects Research (PDF) - August 29, 2002.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must meet NIH requirements for human and animal subjects research; reviewers and applicants must ensure compliance with these requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subject protection and inclusion decision trees
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer Review Decision Trees for Human Subject Protection and Inclusion Issues (Glossary) (PDF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision trees and glossaries are provided to guide reviewers through assessment of protection and inclusion issues (e.g., when protections/inclusion policies apply, how to rate concerns).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of women in clinical research
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy documents: Women in Clinical Research (PDF); Women in NIH-Defined Phase III Clinical Trials (PDF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess whether applications address inclusion of women appropriately per NIH policy; specific guidance is in the linked documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of minorities in clinical research
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy documents: Minorities in Clinical Research (PDF); Minorities in NIH-Defined Phase III Clinical Trials (PDF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are expected to address inclusion of racial/ethnic minorities as appropriate; reviewers use provided documents to evaluate adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of children in human subjects research
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy document: Children in Human Subjects Research (PDF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications involving pediatric populations must follow NIH policy; reviewers evaluate whether inclusion/justification and protections for children are adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plans in clinical trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy document: Data and Safety Monitoring Plans in Clinical Trials (PDF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate whether appropriate data and safety monitoring plans are proposed for clinical trials and whether they meet NIH expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating of grant applications / explicit review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Rating of Grant Applications - NIH Announces New Explicit Statements of Review Criteria, June 1997.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH uses explicit statements of review criteria to rate applications; reviewers should apply these criteria when scoring scientific/technical merit (see linked statement for full criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed peer review regulations (compliance and rulemaking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed Peer Review Regulations (PDF): Scientific Peer Review of Research Grant Applications and Research and Development Contract Projects - Notice of proposed rulemaking, September 21, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory proposals describe procedural and legal requirements for peer review of grant and contract projects; reviewers and administrators must be aware of regulatory context and any rule changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of public representatives/participants in scientific peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Workgroup/topic: Inclusion of Public Representatives/Participants in Scientific Peer Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH examines and issues guidance on when/how public representatives should participate in scientific peer review to provide broader perspectives; this is part of PROG and workgroup activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application referral and peer review information availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional information about application referral & peer review is available from the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) web site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and reviewers should consult CSR for details on referral policies, review assignment, and other procedural guidance.
